title: aspect-ratio
learningObjectives: Explain aspect-ratio and use selectors or sizing rules appropriately.

understand.concept: The aspect-ratio property defines a preferred width-to-height ratio for a box. It can help reserve space for media and cards. The browser uses the ratio when at least one dimension is automatic and the sizing rules allow it to determine the other dimension.
understand.whyItMatters: A stable aspect ratio reduces layout shifts and makes image or video containers predictable. It is a preferred ratio and can interact with min/max constraints and replaced element sizing.
understand.analogy: Aspect ratio is the relationship between the width and height of a frame, like a 16:9 video display.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; selector matching and sizing follow CSS specifications and browser layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The frame keeps a 16:9 preferred ratio as its width changes.

examples.explanation: The frame keeps a 16:9 preferred ratio as its width changes.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example showing the selector or sizing behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a square avatar and a 16:9 video placeholder using aspect-ratio. Test max-width constraints.
practise.independentTask: Build a short example that demonstrates the topic with realistic content. Inspect matched selectors or computed sizes in developer tools.
